prep.what: Implement a durable job queue so the sweeper/daemon pipeline survives restarts and can be observed.
prep.understand: Phase 6 gating item — t21 (sweeper) and t22 (CI lane) both depend on this landing first. The queue must persist across process crashes and expose enough state for the CI lane to query.
approach: Review how jobs are currently enqueued and what data each job carries
Pick a persistence backend (SQLite is already in scope for the project — prefer it over a new dep)
Define the jobs table schema: id, kind, payload JSON, status, created_at, updated_at
Implement enqueue / dequeue / mark-done / mark-failed helpers
Wire the new queue into the existing daemon call-sites, replacing in-memory structures
resources: claude-todos-skill snapshot — tasks list, current phase notes
Existing daemon entrypoint file for call-site map

tasks.title: Writer docker-integration test on a real onboarded repo

prep.what: Prove the writer component works end-to-end inside Docker against a repo that has already gone through onboarding.
prep.understand: Fills the gap between unit tests and the full CI lane. A short task (s=30 min) — pick an already-onboarded repo and assert the writer produces valid output.
approach: Identify the smallest onboarded repo available in the test fixtures
Write a docker-compose or Dockerfile that mounts the repo and runs the writer
Assert the writer exits 0 and the output files match expected structure
Add the test to the existing test suite so it runs in CI
resources: Existing docker test infrastructure if any

prep.what: Add a cross-process lock on the daemon side so concurrent refresh calls from multiple writers/processes can't stomp each other.
prep.understand: Prerequisite for safe concurrent use. Without it two processes refreshing simultaneously corrupt shared cache state.
approach: Identify all code paths that trigger a refresh in the daemon
Choose a lock primitive — SQLite exclusive transaction or a lockfile with fcntl.flock
Wrap the refresh critical section with acquire / release
Write a test that spawns two concurrent refreshers and asserts only one runs at a time
resources: t20 durable job queue (landing earlier today) — may inform lock storage choice

tasks.title: Label lane v2: M3 vision for outlined-text firms + callout-vs-room filtering

prep.what: Upgrade the label detection lane so it correctly classifies outlined-text firms and filters callout labels from room labels.
prep.understand: Currently the label lane conflates callout boxes with room labels. The M3 vision separates them: outlined-text firms get their own detection path, and callout-vs-room filtering happens as a post-classification step.
approach: Review the current label lane pipeline and where firm-type classification happens
Add an outlined-text detector (check for text with outline strokes vs. solid fills)
Implement a callout-vs-room heuristic (callouts typically have leader lines or arrow anchors; rooms are enclosed polygons)
Deploy the MINIMAX_AI key to VPS — t26 may call the vision model for ambiguous cases
Run the label lane against the existing test set and verify precision/recall improves
resources: takeoff-engine snapshot — label lane phase notes, t26 description
MINIMAX_AI API credentials (deploy to VPS before starting)

prep.what: Complete the assemblies-per-room calculation so each room produces paint, drywall, and flooring quantity estimates plus accurate wall heights.
prep.understand: Task is already in_progress — review what's landed and what's still open before writing new code. The core formulas map room geometry (perimeter, area, ceiling height) to assembly quantities.
approach: Read the current in_progress branch/code to see what formulas are already implemented
Identify which of paint / drywall / flooring is missing or incomplete
Implement wall-height extraction from the room geometry (check if ceiling height is detected or needs a default)
Wire the assembly outputs into the per-room result object
Add or extend tests for each assembly type with known-geometry rooms
resources: takeoff-engine snapshot — t18 description, phases 5+6 notes
Existing geometry helpers (perimeter, area calculations already in codebase)
